newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia minister Prosser refuses call to resign.
newsitem.headline: Australia minister Prosser refuses call to resign.

text.p: Australian Small Business Minister Geoff Prosser on Thursday refused demands from the Labor Opposition that he resign from the ministry following controversy surrounding his business interests.

The Opposition has demanded Australian Prime Minister John Howard sack Prosser, saying he had misled parliament, breached ministerial standards and had a possible conflict of interest between his ministerial responsibilities and his day-to-day business dealings.

"I am convinced that I am not in any way engaged in the daily work of the family business and secondly the outline of my corporate structure clearly shows that I am not involved in the daily work of the family," Prosser told parliament.
"I categorically reject any allegations that at any time I have used my ministerial position for personal gain and clearly there is not one shred of evidence to support such an allegation," he said.
Howard has already trimmed the portfolio of Prosser, a businessman who owns shopping malls in Western Australia.
Government guidelines bar ministers from daily business activities and from being involved in decisions which could affect their business interests.

The Opposition has accused Prosser of understating the extent of his dealings with Coles Myers Ltd Deputy Chairman and former senior conservative politician Nick Greiner and of lobbying local government politicians about his businesses.

A junior minister and parliamentary secretary quit last year after allegations of potential conflict of interest and one government member and a recently retired government senator are before the courts on charges of abusing parliamentary benefits.
